summary: Turn a venture thesis into source-labeled assumptions, staged falsification experiments, resource bounds, kill criteria, and decision records.
triggers: A venture thesis needs stress-testing before resources are committed.
Existential assumptions need bounded experiments and decision thresholds.
A product or market plan must preserve unknowns and contradictory evidence.
antiTriggers: Commit funds or give regulated investment advice.
Treat forecasts, enthusiasm, or a prototype as validated demand.
Contact customers or launch an experiment without explicit scope.

provenance.note: Method source read in full and independently rewritten for portable product use; the historical file remains unchanged.
Stage, assumptions, falsification, resource, kill-criteria, and uncertainty semantics informed the rewrite; no source prose was copied.
Ownership and evidence boundaries were consulted; no demand, market, or investment result is asserted.
